audio_script_it:
Buongiorno, benvenuti al Morning Briefing di Price Alert.

Il Nikkei ha chiuso in calo del 2,73%, Shanghai in ribasso dell'1,61%. Questo suggerisce un'apertura debole per i mercati europei.

L'S&P 500 è in calo dell'1,21% a 7.408,30 punti. Il VIX registra un rialzo dell'1,02% a 18,89, segnale di maggiore avversione al rischio. Il Dollar Index è in lieve ribasso dello 0,10% a 101,33. L'oro è stabile, leggero aumento dello 0,08% a quattro mila cinquanta dollari l'oncia. Il Brent scende del 7,97% a novantadue dollari e settantasei centesimi al barile. Il rendimento del Treasury USA a 10 anni è in rialzo dello 0,99% a quattro virgola settanta per cento. Il TLT a 20 anni è in calo dello 0,32% a ottantatré virgola diciassette. Il BTP a 10 anni resta stabile al 3,73%. Lo STOXX 600 guadagna lo 0,36% a sessanta tre virgola novantatré punti, mentre il FTSE MIB avanza dello 0,48% a cinquantuno mila cinquecentotrentuno punti.

Il summit NATO, in corso, riunisce i leader alleati per definire la risposta alle tensioni in Russia e Iran. Le discussioni sulla difesa europea aumentano la pressione sui titoli del settore, mentre le crisi geopolitiche mantengono alta l'incertezza sui mercati energetici. La Banca Centrale Europea ha confermato i tassi invariati, ma ha lanciato un sondaggio per il design delle nuove banconote, segnale di attenzione alla stabilità monetaria.

Nessun dato macro rilevante in uscita oggi.

Passiamo ora al comparto degli asset digitali. Bitcoin si mantiene sopra sessantacinquemila dollari, con variazione positiva di zero virgola zero sei percento. Il flusso giornaliero netto degli ETF è negativo di due milioni di dollari, segnale di lieve pressione di vendita. Nessun driver specifico emerge oltre al contesto geopolitico, ma il prezzo resta stabile. Ethereum registra una discesa di uno virgola zero tre percento, Solana perde uno virgola quarantasei percento e Binance Coin è pressoché invariato con meno di zero virgola un percento. Il Fear & Greed Index segna ventotto, collocandosi nella zona della paura. Questo suggerisce cautela tra gli investitori, con un sentiment teso che potrebbe limitare gli acquisti di nuovo asset.

Nessun dato macro in agenda oggi. Per approfondire i temi di oggi, sulla nostra piattaforma trovate gli articoli completi nella sezione Storie in Primo Piano. Grazie per l'attenzione e a domani
audio_script_en:
Good morning, welcome to the Price Alert Morning Briefing.

The Nikkei closed down 2.73%, Shanghai down 1.61%. This suggests a weak opening for European markets.

The S&P 500 is down 1.21% at 7,408.3 points. The VIX is up 1.02% at 18.89, signaling higher risk aversion. The Dollar Index is slightly down 0.1% at 101.33. Gold is flat, a modest rise of 0.08% at $4,050 per ounce. Brent falls 7.97% to $92.76 per barrel. The 10-year U.S. Treasury yield is up 0.99% at 4.7%. The 20-year TLT is down 0.32% at 83.17. The 10-year BTP remains stable at 3.73%. The STOXX 600 gains 0.36% to 63.93 points, while the FTSE MIB advances 0.48% to 51,531 points.

The NATO summit, ongoing, gathers allied leaders to define the response to tensions in Russia and Iran. Discussions on European defence increase pressure on sector stocks, while geopolitical crises keep energy‑market uncertainty high. The European Central Bank has kept rates unchanged but launched a survey on new banknote designs, a sign of focus on monetary stability.

No significant macro data scheduled for release today.

Let's pivot to the cryptocurrency markets... Bitcoin remains above $65,000, with a positive change of 0.06%. Net daily ETF flow is negative $2 million, indicating slight selling pressure. No specific driver emerges beyond the geopolitical backdrop, but the price stays stable. Ethereum is down 0.03%, Solana loses 1.46% and Binance Coin is essentially flat with less than 0.1% movement. The Fear & Greed Index sits at 28, placing it in fear territory. This suggests caution among investors, with a tense sentiment that could curb new asset purchases.

No macro data on the agenda today. For a deeper dive into today’s topics, visit our platform and find the full articles in the Featured Stories section. Thank you for listening and see you tomorrow.

articles.title: The Strong Suffer What They Must
articles.snippet: Foolish military interventions driven by outdated calculations of economic power have thoroughly discredited the old big powers. Thucydides might well have appreciated the irony of a world in which smaller, weaker countries like Ukraine and Iran can expose Russia and the United States, respectively, as paper tigers.

articles.title: Rethinking Global Imbalances
articles.snippet: Today’s global imbalances, starting with China's massive trade surplus, are not simply the result of poor macroeconomic coordination. Rather, they reflect long-term strategic thinking and a departure from the bias toward openness on which the postwar trade order was built.

articles.title: Are Trump administration policies catalyzing European unity?
articles.snippet: The second Trump administration has signaled occasional hostility to Europeans and the European Union in ways unprecedented in American government practice since the beginnings of European integration in the 1950s. At the same time, the European Union has embarked on new initiatives that express unity and clarity of purpose, such as a $100 billion commitment of financial assistance to Ukraine, including for military purposes, and the conclusion of a landmark trade agreement with the South American customs union Mercosur. Is America's intermittent adversarial stance weakening or strengthening…

articles.title: Commodities Beat Tech This Decade, and Wall Street Still Won't Buy In
articles.snippet: The best performing asset class of this decade is also the most under owned. Since October 2020, when we first called for a decades-long super-cycle in commodities, the broad commodity indices like the S&P GSCI are up 200 per cent; gold 140 per cent. This year commodities are up 37 per cent with petroleum up 81 per cent. The bottlenecks rotated – gold, copper, silver, coffee, cocoa, oil and most recently diesel. But not the trend. In contrast, crypto indices are up 157 per cent, the Nasdaq 145 per cent and the S&P 500 117 per cent.…

articles.title: Ukraine’s Drone War Is Choking Kazakhstan’s Oil Exports
articles.snippet: Kazakhstan should, in theory, be one of the major beneficiaries of Russia’s growing isolation from global energy markets. Its crude is unsanctioned and European refiners need alternatives to Russian barrels. Yet instead of gaining a clear geopolitical advantage, Kazakhstan has found itself exposed to many of the same risks as its northern neighbour: attacks on export infrastructure, disruptions inside Russia and repeated operational failures at its own largest fields.
